metadata.title: Milky Way Mass Models for Orbit Calculations

evidence.quote: hypervelocity star HE 0437-5439 is investigated again to check its suggested origin in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC).

When hypervelocity stars were first discovered in 2005
(Brown et al. 2005), dynamical ejection from the supermassive
black hole at the GC (Hills 1988) was supposed to be their only
origin because these stars move so fast that they are unbound
to the Galaxy. This scenario was challenged by the discovery of the
third hypervelocity star HE 0437-5439 (Edelmann et al. 2005), a
massive B star

Finally, the enigmatic hypervelocity star HE 0437-5439 is
re-investigated by inspecting its trajectory in the context of the
updated potentials.

notes: HE 0437-5439 is included as a follow-up: it is explicitly identified as a previously known hypervelocity star and is reanalyzed here to test its LMC versus GC origin. J1539+0239 (SDSSJ153935.67+023909.8) was not included: although T:p5-b12 and T:p8-b2 report unbound best-fitting-model orbits, the paper selects it by requiring it to be gravitationally bound (T:p1-b15; T:p3-b15) and treats the nonzero χ* values as tolerated constraint violations caused by large errors, rather than retaining an unbound candidacy.

HE 0437-5439: Table 4 lists HE 0437-5439's proper-motion uncertainties as separate statistical and systematic 1σ terms; both are retained in the error field rather than combined. The supplied material does not report a parallax, present-day Galactocentric radius, total Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HE 0437-5439.
